title: Low sleep and high soreness deload protocol
recommended_actions: Replace heavy resistance work for the affected muscle group with active recovery.
Use easy aerobic work, breathing drills, and low-load mobility for 20 to 35 minutes.
Keep intensity conversational and stop if soreness changes into sharp pain.
avoid: Heavy compound lifts for the sore muscle group.
escalation: If soreness is paired with sharp pain, swelling, limping, or worsening night pain, recommend professional medical evaluation.

title: Elevated resting heart rate and stress downshift
recommended_actions: Reduce the day's planned training intensity by one level.
Favor technique work, zone 2 cardio, mobility, or an upper-body session if lower-body fatigue is also present.
Keep sets below RPE 7 and increase rest periods.
avoid: Hard intervals when stress and resting heart rate are both elevated.
escalation: If elevated heart rate is unusual, persistent, or paired with illness symptoms, recommend rest and professional guidance.

title: Low blood oxygen low-intensity protocol
recommended_actions: Keep activity low intensity and conservative.
Prefer walking, gentle mobility, or complete rest depending on symptoms.
Do not use the reading alone as diagnosis; treat it as a demo safety signal.
avoid: Training through shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, or unusual symptoms.
escalation: If low blood oxygen is persistent or paired with shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, or blue lips, recommend urgent medical evaluation.

title: Pain safety stop rule
recommended_actions: Replace the session with rest, gentle range-of-motion, or non-painful low-impact activity.
Keep any movement below mild discomfort.
avoid: Training through sharp, stabbing, or constant pain.
Loading a joint that is hot, red, swollen, or causing a limp.
Repeating the same exercise that caused worsening symptoms.
escalation: Recommend professional medical evaluation when pain is sharp, causes limping, lasts more than two hours after exercise, worsens at night, or swelling does not improve.

title: High step count lower-body volume reduction
recommended_actions: Reduce additional lower-body volume when high steps combine with quad or calf soreness.
Use mobility, trunk work, upper-body training, or easy cycling instead of extra loaded lower-body sets.
Maintain movement quality and avoid chasing volume on fatigued legs.
avoid: High-rep squats or lunges after a high-activity day.
Adding extra finishers for the same muscle group.
escalation: If high activity is paired with pain, swelling, or altered gait, follow the pain safety stop rule.

title: Green readiness normal progression
recommended_actions: Proceed with the planned training session.
Progress load only when technique is stable and working sets stay at or below the target RPE.
Keep the normal warm-up and cool-down in place.
avoid: Skipping warm-up because readiness is high.
Large load jumps without recent performance evidence.
escalation: If pain or unusual symptoms appear during the session, override GREEN status and follow the relevant safety rule.
